quotations.old_english: Swá þ-bar; wæs æteówed, þ-bar; hé bródette byfiende mid wundorlicre styrunge
quotations.latin: ut apparuerit cancussione mirifica tremendo palpitasse

quotations.old_english: Þá ongan hé ofdrǽdd bifian and broddettan (forhtiende and brédetende, v. l.) and clypian . . . Hí þone munuc cwakiendne and broddettendne (bród-, v. l.) gelǽddon
quotations.latin: coepit ipse tremens et palpitans clamare . . . trementem et palpitantem monachum reduxerunt

quotations.old_english: Brogdetende vel cleppetende campus (can the English words be epithets applied to campus ( = aequor, cf. Corp. Gl. H. A. 314, aequor, pelagus vel campus) referring to the quivering of the surface of the water?)
Mid dislicum glengcgum brottetende (v. brogdettung for form)

source_text: brogdettan (brodd-, bród-, bréd-, brott- ?); p. te. I. to shake, quiver :-- Brogdetteð vibrat, Txts. 107, 2132. Swá þ-bar; wæs æteówed, þ-bar; hé bródette byfiende mid wundorlicre styrunge ut apparuerit cancussione mirifica tremendo palpitasse, Gr. D. 166, 14. Þá ongan hé ofdrǽdd bifian and broddettan (forhtiende and brédetende, v. l.) and clypian . . . Hí þone munuc cwakiendne and broddettendne (bród-, v. l.) gelǽddon coepit ipse tremens et palpitans clamare . . . trementem et palpitantem monachum reduxerunt, 156, 13-21. Brogdetende vel cleppetende campus (can the English words be epithets applied to campus ( = aequor, cf. Corp. Gl. H. A. 314, aequor, pelagus vel campus) referring to the quivering of the surface of the water?), Txts. 49, 411. Brogdetende, brocdaettendi, brogdaethendi palpitans, 83, 1472. Bródetende, Wrt. Voc. ii. 67, 54. II. to glitter, be splendid (cf. brogdian) :-- Mid dislicum glengcgum brottetende (v. brogdettung for form) stolidis pompis indruticans, Hpt. Gl. 435, 37.
